an3.25:2.1: The Pali word for “lighting” (_vijju_, Sanskrit _vidyut_) is similar to “knowledge” (_vijjā_), albeit from a different root.
an3.25:2.3: This is in reference to the experience of stream-entry. This vision of the four noble truths occurs in a flash that is unmistakable and unforgettable. The nature of the world is revealed in all its clarity. Yet the stream-enterer still has fetters, so their direct vision of the truth is transitory. But like a person wandering in the dark, who all of a sudden sees what is around them revealed by lightning, they never go back to the same level of ignorance.
an3.25:3.1: The Pali word for “diamond” (_vajira_, Sanskrit _vajra_) is similar to that for “lightning”, and indeed is sometimes used in the sense of “thunderbolt”. However the simile makes the meaning clear.
